question: The analgesic effects of morphine are mediated primarily through agonism at the mu (μ) opioid receptor.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Morphine and most clinical opioids (codeine, oxycodone, fentanyl) act principally at μ receptors. Kappa (κ) receptors contribute to spinal analgesia and dysphoria; delta (δ) receptors modulate mood and analgesia but are less clinically targeted.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The μ receptor (OPRM1) is the primary target for morphine and most clinically used opioids. It mediates supraspinal and spinal analgesia, but also euphoria, respiratory depression, and constipation — explaining the opioid side-effect profile.
